subsystems.name: Telescope
subsystems.role: collects infrared light from both the planet and its host star with an off-axis design that keeps the star's light out of the science beam.
parts: elliptical primary mirror about 1.1 by 0.7 m

subsystems.name: Spectrometer
subsystems.role: splits the combined starlight-plus-planet light into a spectrum across the mid-infrared.

subsystems.name: Fine guidance and photometers
subsystems.role: holds the star precisely on the detector and records its visible and near-infrared brightness as a reference.

subsystems.name: Payload module and thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps the optics and detectors cold without consuming cryogen so their own glow does not swamp the signal.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the payload, points it, powers it and sends data home.
parts: attitude control thrusters and reaction wheels

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: turns raw detector counts into atmospheric abundances.

buildSteps.title: Set the science requirements
buildSteps.detail: Engineers fix the wavelength range, spectral resolution and photometric stability needed to detect a planet's atmosphere, since these set every later design choice.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the mirrors
buildSteps.detail: An off-axis mirror is machined, diamond-turned and polished, then coated, because the off-axis shape avoids the central obstruction that would scatter starlight.

buildSteps.title: Build the telescope structure
buildSteps.detail: Mirrors and mounts are assembled on a bench made of the same aluminium alloy, so the whole assembly shrinks uniformly when cooled and stays in focus.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the instruments
buildSteps.detail: The spectrometer, detectors and photometer channels are mounted on the bench and aligned under cleanroom conditions to micron tolerances.

buildSteps.title: Wrap it in thermal shielding
buildSteps.detail: Sunshield and radiating panels are fitted so that the payload can radiate its own heat to deep space and settle near 50 K passively.

buildSteps.title: Mate payload and spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: The payload module is bolted onto the bus carrying solar arrays, thrusters, avionics and communications.

buildSteps.title: Test as a whole
buildSteps.detail: The assembled observatory goes through vibration, acoustic and thermal-vacuum testing that mimics launch and the cold of space.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: After reaching the Sun–Earth L2 point, the observatory cools down, the optics are focused, and calibration stars are used to verify stability before the survey begins.

buildSteps.title: Run the survey
buildSteps.detail: Each target is observed repeatedly through transits, eclipses and full orbits, building up a spectrum from the tiny difference between starlight alone and starlight plus planet.

prerequisites.why: infrared telescopes such as Herschel and JWST showed that shielding and radiators alone can hold optics cold enough to observe faint infrared signals.
the spectrometer needs detectors sensitive to single photons across the mid-infrared while staying stable over long exposures.
Hubble and JWST have measured individual exoplanet atmospheres, proving the method but not yet at population scale.

prerequisites.tech: A large catalogue of well-characterised exoplanets
prerequisites.why: the mission needs hundreds of planets with known orbits, sizes and host-star properties to schedule and interpret observations.
the signal is a fraction of a percent of the starlight, so the star must stay on the same detector pixels for hours.

pathway.milestone: assembling and testing the observatory while the target list is refined
pathway.unlocks: a defined survey sample and a launch-ready instrument.

pathway.milestone: launch to L2 and in-orbit commissioning
pathway.unlocks: confirmation that the passively cooled optics reach their design sensitivity.

pathway.milestone: a survey of roughly a thousand transiting planets over a few years
pathway.unlocks: comparisons between planet types rather than one-off measurements.

pathway.milestone: population results linking atmospheric composition to how planets formed and migrated
pathway.unlocks: statistical constraints that feed the next generation of missions.

pathway.milestone: spectroscopy of smaller, cooler, potentially habitable planets
pathway.unlocks: requires larger apertures, active cooling or starlight suppression beyond current designs.
